claims.text: An AlCoCrFeNi-based eutectic high-entropy alloy is a candidate interlayer material.
A thin, coherent AlCoCrFeNi-based eutectic interlayer can moderate the transition from diffusion-mediated to dislocation-mediated creep in HEA multilayers.
The coherent interlayer will suppress excessive atomic diffusion at lower temperatures.
The interlayer will permit diffusional accommodation at high temperatures and thereby make the creep-mechanism transition gradual.
The initial HEA multilayers may have semi-coherent or incoherent interfaces.
The initial HEA multilayers primarily exhibit diffusion-mediated creep at high homologous temperatures.
The proposed AlCoCrFeNi-based interlayer can be engineered to maintain high coherency with adjacent HEA layers.
A coherently bonded ultrathin interlayer will maintain lattice continuity and reduce local interface diffusivity.
Matching lattice parameters reduces effective interface diffusion paths and lowers vacancy diffusion and diffusion creep at lower temperatures.
At higher temperatures, the coherent interlayer retains sufficient atomic mobility for diffusion creep.
Maintaining interface coherency reduces barriers to dislocation motion and facilitates dislocation nucleation.
The modified multilayer will have a measurably lower creep rate at lower temperatures than a multilayer without the interlayer.
The lower creep rate at lower temperatures will result from enhanced dislocation activity.
The modified multilayer will exhibit a distinct change in creep activation energy indicating a transition from diffusional to dislocation-mediated creep.
Multilayers without the engineered interlayer will retain higher diffusion-dominated creep rates across the tested temperature range.
The transition effect requires an interlayer thin enough to preserve coherency.
Avoiding secondary-phase formation at the interface is necessary for the proposed transition effect.
Extreme temperatures or substantial interlayer-thickness deviations may make the mechanism transition less distinct.
AlCoCrFeNi2.1 is a eutectic high-entropy alloy containing a B2 body-centered-cubic phase.

contradictions.description: The predicted lower-temperature creep-rate reduction is attributed to enhanced dislocation activity, while the mechanism also describes reduced vacancy diffusion as the relevant rate-reducing effect. The respective causal contributions are not reconciled, and enhanced dislocation activity would not by itself clearly imply a lower creep rate.

The baseline is said to remain diffusion-dominated across the entire temperature range, whereas the initial-state and conditions fields restrict diffusion-mediated dominance to high temperatures and anticipate increasing dislocation-mediated behavior at lower temperatures.
